key_insight: A composite online-to-nonconvex conversion method can achieve optimal oracle complexity for stochastic nonsmooth nonconvex optimization with a convex regularizer, matching the best known noncomposite rates.
engineering_relevance: This gives a theoretically optimal recipe for training regularized machine-learning models and solving constrained engineering problems under noisy gradient or function-value access.
method: Use an online learner to choose update directions in a nonconvex optimization loop.
Modify the online losses so the convex regularizer appears directly rather than being linearized.
Apply a low-regret online mirror descent variant to obtain Goldstein-type stationarity guarantees.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports oracle complexity guarantees of O(δ^-1 ε^-3) stochastic gradient queries or O(d δ^-1 ε^-3) function-value queries, plus smooth-case rates and numerical experiments.
watch_item: The guarantees target Goldstein-type stationarity, so practical performance may depend on tuning the radius δ and on how well the stochastic oracle matches the theory.
paper_title: Composite Online-to-Nonconvex Conversion with Optimal Oracle Complexity
